title: Recording: Single Pigeon by Wings | 1972
content:
Studio One, Olympic Studios, London
Producer: Glyn Johns
Engineer: Phil Chapman

Wings began recording ‘Single Pigeon’ for their second album Red Rose Speedway on 9 March 1972.

I had seen a single pigeon, just pecking around – a blue-grey pigeon on its own near some railings – and I thought the combination of those words was quite winning: ‘single pigeon’. I began to think about why the pigeon might be single.

The minute you decide to make up a story about a pigeon, it’s not just a pigeon. It’s a character in a play. It’s a guy who’s had an argument with his girl the night before, and he’s got chucked out of the house. So here he is. He’s single now. All because of the ‘Sunday morning fight about Saturday night’.

Paul McCartney
The Lyrics: 1956 To The Present

The backing track had Paul McCartney on piano and vocals, Henry McCullough on acoustic guitar, Denny Laine on drums, and Wings’ normal drummer Denny Seiwell on bass guitar.

Session producer Glyn Johns grew frustrated during the session, not least Wings’ unprofessionalism in the studio. The musicians were stoned and not taking the process seriously, and Johns left the project at the end of March 1972.

They wanted to enjoy themselves in the studio. They obviously like to take their time over recording. I’d say ‘fantastic’ if I could see a good end result emerging. Their idea of having a good time isn’t mine necessarily, that’s the point.
Glyn Johns
Melody Maker, 22 April 1972

Overdubs were added at Abbey Road on 29 January 1973. Again, it was an unusual session, involving the members of Wings playing unconventional instruments: McCartney played a trombone, Laine was on saxophone, and Seiwell played a cornet.
